reasoning_traces.think:
The access control matrix partitions implementation into two regimes: low-impact incremental improvements (allowed list) and high-impact transformative deployments (approval required). This mirrors the statistical distinction between exploratory data analysis (where we generate hypotheses) and confirmatory hypothesis testing (where we validate those hypotheses with new data). The allowed list corresponds to regions of parameter space where prior knowledge (design tokens, components) remains valid, while the approval required list demands fresh evidence generation. The approval protocol hierarchy introduces a graded escalation of scrutiny, analogous to sequential hypothesis testing where each level raises the bar for significance. Both primitives enforce a form of computational irreducibility: the full consequences of a deployment cannot be deduced solely from its individual components but must be evaluated holistically. In GSI, this manifests as the need to verify that cloned interfaces preserve the underlying probabilistic structure of the original platform. In GSE, it translates to ensuring that state transitions respect the causal graph of the application.
